items.title: Federal judge declines to intervene in Cigna’s refusal to pay $3M No Surprises Act award - HealthExec
items.reason: This item directly addresses federal litigation over No Surprises Act enforcement, specifically a court ruling on an IDR award payment dispute involving a major insurer.
items.summary: A federal judge declined to order Cigna to pay a $3 million Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) award under the No Surprises Act, refusing to intervene in the insurer's refusal to comply with the award. The ruling represents a significant judicial development in enforcement of the No Surprises Act's IDR process, which is designed to resolve balance-billing disputes between insurers and providers. This outcome directly affects how revenue-cycle teams can pursue IDR awards and whether court intervention is available to compel payment when insurers refuse to honor IDR determinations.
